assertions.name: A1_chain_attachment_is_exactly_rank_one
assertions.source: spread 3.886e-16 over 20 prefixes; matches F_pp to 2.3e-13

assertions.name: A5_no_decay_and_subadditivity_are_one_fact
assertions.source: far p-n bond matches adjacent p-n to 1.1e-15 while the triangle defect is -0.236512

assertions.name: A6_alpha_free_shortfall_of_two_point_one
assertions.source: model ratio <= 6.0643 vs AME 12.7196, short 2.0975x, alpha-independent

description: Locates the many-body term, measures its sign, and derives an alpha-free ceiling that puts 4He out of reach of the bond graph. The chain (k=1) attachment functional P -> tr(P.A)/tr(P) is exactly rank one — one constant over 20 random prefixes to <1e-12, independently reproducing the arc's recorded F_pp = 0.385581983466. The all-pairs (k=2) attachment is not: the same prefixes give 0.196..0.696. The mechanism is the band generator (T5 T4 T3)(T2+d)(T3 T4 T5)^-1, which routes strand 2 through strands 3-5 — the middle nucleon — so a non-adjacent bond does not commute past the prefix. That failure to commute IS the three-body term. It is NEGATIVE in all eight A=3 flavour orderings (-9.04% to -15.04% of the naive sum), i.e. it REMOVES binding. It also privileges the middle nucleon: reversal is exact (pnn vs nnp, 0.0) but permutation is not (pnp vs ppn 4.17%, npn vs nnp 5.05% on identical bond multisets), a labelling artifact of embedding the bond graph in a line. This explains rather than contradicts no-distance-decay: the bond's own invariant is routing-independent while its commutator with what it passes through is not. Ceiling: B(2H) is exact at A=2 (single bond, no many-body term possible) and the naive B(4He) contains no many-body term at all, giving B(4He)/B(2H) <= 6.0643 against AME 12.7196 — short by 2.0975x with alpha cancelling, so no normalisation fixes it, and closing it would need large POSITIVE many-body terms where all eight measured are negative.
caveats: THE CEILING IS A ONE-SIDED BOUND WITH ONE UNMEASURED INPUT. B(2H) is exact — a single bond admits no many-body term. The B(4He) figure is the naive pairwise sum, which contains no many-body term at all, so it is an upper bound PROVIDED the A=4 many-body terms are non-positive. That is measured for all eight THREE-body terms at A=3 and NOT measured for the genuine FOUR-body term, which needs H_12. The unconditional statement is the weaker and still sufficient one: a pairwise sum with no many-body content gives 6.0643 against 12.7196, and every many-body term measured so far has the sign that makes it worse.

'Rank one' here is a statement about the functional P -> tr(P.A) restricted to the prefix subalgebra, measured on 20 random words plus the physical configurations — not a proved algebraic rank. The k=1 result is exact to 1e-12 across every prefix tried, which is what the telescoping argument in chain_telescopes_and_ordering_sensitivity_probe already rests on; this reproduces it independently and contrasts it with k=2.

A=3 traces here are H_9 seminormal and the A=2 bond constants are read off the same machinery, matching the arc's independently recorded L_pp / L_pn / L_nn to all printed digits. Everything is the FRAMED convention (-log(z+d), no writhe normalisation); the framed/normalised choice moves these numbers by 1-3 %, which does not approach the 2.1x shortfall and so cannot affect the conclusion.
